log: 343 of the 344 meshes (all with empty material name) have byte-identical evidence: 1800 triangles, one island, size 2.000x2.000x1.989, at 0.50,0.50,0.50, no texture, no colour. Position, size, colour and material give nothing that separates one from another, so no function can be justified for any of them.

Rule: each such mesh is a `whole` part named Near_Cubic_Unit_<tag> (shape-descriptive only: bounding box nearly cubic, centred, uncoloured), group Near_Cubic_Unit_Group_<tag>. <tag> is a 3-letter base-26 code of the mesh's order among these meshes (Aaa, Aab, ...); it carries NO evidence and exists only because names must be unique and numbered placeholders are barred. This is an abstention for all of them.

Because every mesh is centred on the same point at the same size, they are presumably stacked or are copies of one shape at different transforms; the evidence has no world position per mesh to place them left/right/high/low, so even location words could not be used.

The one mesh with material 'Guides Material' is 3 flat (zero-thickness) black 2-triangle strips, 24 long: one along x (at y 0.96), one along y (at x 0.03), one along z (at x 0.97). Named by axis direction and `at` position only; classes guide/line from shape (flat, long, thin) and the material name (used as evidence, not listed in basis). 'High/Low' in names are relative positions within the mesh, not world positions.

Plan syntax: no trouble; the guide has no `source` requirement on my side (added for me). Cost: generating 343 unjustifiable names is the real problem, the format has no way to say 'unnamed/abstain' beyond a made-up unique name.
